newsitem.title: USA: Perry says Iraq, Iran seek control of Gulf oil.
newsitem.headline: Perry says Iraq, Iran seek control of Gulf oil.

text.p: U.S. Defence Secretary William Perry told U.S. sailors patrolling the Gulf on Friday that their job was to stop Iraq and Iran from seeking to control world oil supplies.
"I don't have to tell you who those two nations are; they are Iraq and Iran," Perry told the crew of aircraft carrier USS Kitty Hawk which entered the Gulf earlier this month.
"Two countries" had designs on controlling "two-thirds of world oil supplies located in the Gulf," Perry said.
"There is nothing more intimidating than a carrier battle group. That is your job -- to intimidate Iraq and Iran."
Iran, the region's non-Arab power, is strategically placed at the entrance to the Gulf, the narrow Strait of Hormuz, through which 15 million barrels of oil pass daily.
Western powers and their Gulf Arab allies have in recent months repeatedly expressed concern over Iran's rearmament programme, saying it was a threat to the oil-rich region.
The United States has 27 warships in and around the Gulf as part of a "dual containment" policy to deter Iran and Kuwait's former occupier Iraq.
